cells.tense: You read the space between people and give it a shape to move through, right here, with the pen in hand.
cells.ask: Before your next gathering, shape one small thing — a way in, a seat, an order — and let that shape carry the tone instead of you.
cells.core: You hold the shape of a room while it fills. Not the loudest one in it and not a guest waiting for someone else to set the tone — you build the frame that feeling moves through, and people settle into it without wondering why. That isn't softness. It's architecture, done warmly.\n\nWhat keeps it working is holding without gripping. You notice how people are doing, you set the container a beat before it's needed, and you don't make anyone pay for not fitting it. That's the whole art, and you have it. The next move is to build one thing that holds on its own — something in the shape of the room that carries it when you step away.
cells.sheetLine: You give feeling a shape to move through, and you do it well.
cells.verb: Steward of Resonance (Agent) — tending the space between people so feeling can move through it

cells.tense: You're already arranging how it will land, rehearsing the tone of a moment that hasn't arrived.
cells.ask: Let one gathering start without your plan, and stay in it ten minutes before you adjust anything.
cells.core: You're managing how it's going to go before it starts. Who'll need drawing out, where the awkwardness sits, which feeling has to be stayed ahead of — the shape is built in advance, and the real moment keeps arriving to find you already finished with it. Holding a room has turned into running it.\n\nWhat you're after is to be met, not obeyed, and a plan this complete leaves nobody room to meet you. The tone you keep adjusting comes from your grip on something that hasn't happened yet. Set the room up, then step into it with your hands open — leave one thing unscheduled and let the first minutes carry themselves.
cells.sheetLine: You're arranging the room before the room has a chance to happen.

cells.tense: You feel the room and stay out of it, standing at a doorway while the gathering moves on past you.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing you notice about how they're doing, out loud, before the week ends.
cells.core: You can feel what's moving between people and you're not doing anything with it. Stepping in went quiet somewhere, so the reading still happens and the shaping doesn't — you've gone silent in rooms you could be steadying, and nobody is asking you to. It isn't feeling that's absent.\n\nWhat's missing is the small structure that lets feeling land: reading a person and putting one thing in place around them. Run well, this looks like saying one plain true thing and letting that be enough, not opening anything large. It's the same act as before, just smaller. Nothing has to be repaired by it. You do it today for your own practice, not for the room.
cells.sheetLine: You feel what's moving and you've stopped doing anything with it.

cells.tense: In most rooms, you set the pace while telling yourself the room set it on its own.
cells.ask: In one conversation, say plainly — to yourself or to someone there — that you were the one reading the mood and steering it.
cells.core: Something in you tracks a room — the pace, what gets said, what gets left alone — and when you describe it, it comes out as the room did it, the timing did it, the comfort simply happened. The steering runs and stays unnamed, and nobody needs to correct you about your own experience.\n\nWhat this looks like when it's working is knowing you were the one who made it land, and saying so once, plainly. It's a small sentence and it's the whole distance. Say it to yourself if nobody else is there. It stays yours either way, and it's true either way.
cells.sheetLine: You're already keeping the peace. You just haven't claimed it.
cells.verb: Steward of Resonance (Agent) — tending the space between people so feeling can move through it
